analytic.title: An Improved Rate-Monotonic Scheduler and a Real-time Open Control Platform for Robotic Control Algorithm Verification *

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: The verification of new intelligent robotic control algorithm not only requires the correction of computation but also satisfies the timing constraints. In this paper, an open realtime control environment is designed and implemented for robotic control algorithm verification. With Windows NT's real time extension RTX, the PC based control system will have good real-time performance for new control algorithm research. The software structure and the task scheduling approach are described in detail and the software comprises of real-time motion control & trajectory planning process, the use's operating interface process and the inter-process communication module. Considering the uncertainty in computation time of complex intelligent algorithms in robotic systems, the running time of the algorithm is monitored online and an improved rate-monotonic scheduler is presented for schedulability verification. To prove the effectiveness of the open real-time control environment and task scheduler, two examples, a direct driven air-bearing stage for IC packaging and a SCARA type robot for assembly, are introduced. The control performance and task scheduling results show that the open real time control environment and new scheduler are successful in complex control algorithm research and timing verification.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Due to the complexity of robotic system and the necessity of more intelligence for autonomous behavior in changing environment, many advanced control algorithms such as neural nets, fuzzy logic and genetic algorithms are widely used in robotic control system. Although they appear as a promising approach to cope with the nonlinearities and complexity of systems to be controlled, the timing constraints for running the algorithms should be satisfied. That means, the verification of a new intelligent control algorithm includes two steps, the first is the verification of the correction and the effectiveness of the algorithm by simulation; the second is to verify whether the control algorithm gets the computation results in time under the support of an effective scheduling policy and a real-time software environment. In this paper, a real-time control platform and a task scheduler will be introduced for the timing verification of an intelligent algorithm and furthermore, two examples of air-bearing stage for IC packaging and a SCARA type robot for assembly will be discussed in detail.

In robotic control system, most of the advanced control algorithms require open control architectures support where software modules can be modified and exteroceptive sensors like force/torque sensors and vision systems can be easily integrated. Various open control architectures for robots, which can be mainly classified to multiprocessor systems and single processor systems, have already been developed by robot and control manufacturers as well as in research labs [1] [2]. A multiprocessor system, consisting of more than one processor for both complex kinematic and dynamic computation and multi-axis real time control, were widely adopted in robot control systems in the past, although this architecture have deterministic response for real-time control and powerful floating point computation capability for multisensor intelligent control algorithm, it has the deficiency of complexity, high cost and lack of flexibility, and most important, the key components of the software are proprietary and can not be modified by the user, so it is not suitable for development of new control algorithm.

The alternative scenario is adopting standard PC hardware and a standard operating system such as MS-DOS, Linux or MS-Windows. A PC based controller can more easily integrate many commercially available add-on peripherals, such as mass storage devices, ethernet card and other I/O devices. Moreover, standard software development tools (e.g., Visual C++, Visual Basic, Delphi, etc.) can be utilized.

An important issue of control software architectures deals with real-time operating systems. There are many hard realtime control systems available in research lab such as QNX [3], RT-Linux [4], RTX [5] for windows and so on, under which the non-real-time tasks and real-time control algorithm can be executed concurrently. In this paper, an environment of open real-time control for the research of advanced control algorithms is presented. The hardware of control system is based on PC architecture and general I/O devices, so it can be easily added, modified or deleted. The software is based on Windows NT operating system, which is a popular, friendly environment for user-machine interface. To meet the real-time requirements of control algorithm, a real-time extension 978-1-4244-1758-2/08/$25.00 © 2008 IEEE. environment, RTX, is adopted for servo control, sensor sampling, trajectory planning and other real-time tasks.

One of the most important modules in a real-time system is the scheduler. This module is in charge of providing suitable computational resources to the system task set. The ratemonotonic scheduling policy is mostly common used in robotic control system and has been much studied since Liu and Layland in 1973 [6] and the schedulability analysis of sets of independent tasks is based on the fixed execution time or the worst case executing time is predicable [7] [8]. However, it is difficult to predict the response time of advanced intelligent algorithms, or too pessimistic to schedule it under the current rate-monotonic scheduling policy.

To overcome the varying and unpredictable runtime of new intelligent algorithm, in this paper an improved ratemonotonic scheduling approach is presented, by which the time slots of intelligent algorithm in motion control thread is monitored and the schedulability decision function is defined and calculated online, The timing verification of the control algorithm is implemented with the improved scheduling policy.

The paper is organized as follows: in section 2, the software architecture of the open real-time control system will be introduced, in section 3 and 4, the rate-monotonic scheduling will be discussed and a improved approach will be presented for verification of intelligent control algorithms. In last section, the control system of an air bearing stage and a SCARA type assembly robot are described and the scheduling results will be shown.

div.head: II. Overview of the Open Real-time Control System
Hardware System
div.p: The robotic control system for advanced algorithm research comprise an Intel Pentium CPU running the Windows NT operating system, a real time subsystem-RTX, produced by Venturcom's company, is used for real time work. RTX enables application components or modules that require deterministic and high-speed response times, along with other non-real-time application components, to work together on a common Windows NT system. As a hard real-time environment, RTX offers key real-time features, such as deterministic response for periodic processes, high precision timer (resolution 0.1us), controllable priority class (from lowest level 0 to highest 127) and various inter-process communication way (including shared memory, event, semaphore, etc) [9]. Moreover, the developing environment of RTX is very similar to Microsoft Visual C++, which can reduce the development time dramatically.

In hardware design, the single processor architecture is adopted, in which a motion control card is used to sampling linear encoder of servo motors and send an analogue output signal to motor driver as a velocity command. Normally the servo motor driver has a DSP in charge of axis current and velocity closed loop control and the limit position signal and other protecting relay signal will be read via digital I/O channel. The control system outline is shown in fig. 1. Due to the scalability of the standard PC platform, additional hardware can be added to the system easily. For example, external sensors such as force sensor, temperature sensor, air pressure sensor and so on will be treated as analogue signal, they will be integrated to host computer easily with A/D converter.

div.head: Software System
div.p: The software is divided into several modules by functional and logical requirements and the modules are arranged in two processes: real-time process in RTSS environment and non real-time process in Win32 environment. The application module exists in Win32 environment and provides an interface for user to monitor system, manage system and setup motion parameters. All the tasks in this module are non-real-time and have the lowest priority. There are four modules in real-time environment: task scheduling, sensor feedback, trajectory planning and servo control module. Task scheduling module receives the command from application module and decides whether the trajectory planning task starts, the servo control module and the trajectory planning module are periodic tasks to finish calculating the desired position of each axis, sampling the sensors and sending the outputs to servo drivers. Non realtime modules and real-time modules exchange data through Inter-process communication. With shared memory, the key motion related data are exchanged between the two processes. The architecture is shown in fig. 2. Client /server model is adopted in the communication module. Each component of application module has a shared memory with a unique ID. By calling the SendTo function, the application module generates a command data buffer and index information, including source communication ID, destination communication ID, pointer of command data and size of command data. The Getdata function is waiting for the mutex of reading the command data, if the new data incomes to the command buffer, it's copied to local buffer firstly and waits for the attention of scheduling module. On the other hand, the robot state data and sensor information will be transferred to another communication buffer by calling the same SendTo function running in the real-time environment and the application module will receive the state data and display on the screen. z Task scheduling module When receiving the command data from application module, the task scheduling module analyzes the command and then triggers corresponding components to execute the commands. As to direct control commands such as controller configuration, system initialization, quit system, external sensor acquisition and so on, task scheduling module will execute them directly and return the results to the corresponding component of the application module. The axis motion status safety check is executed in servo control module and includes the velocity, motion range, planning step and so on. The control algorithm calculates the output of velocity of axis motor and sends it to the motor driver through D/A converter. At the end of the servo control thread, a servo control finish event is set to notify other process for system control. z Sensor feedback module

To feedback some internal and external information of the robotic system to user, sensor feedback module samples the sensor periodically and transfer the data to user console through a special memory block, which enable user to monitor the current status of robot or save them to data files. III. Improved Rate-Monotonic Scheduler

div.head: Overview of rate0monotonic scheduler
div.p: The problem of scheduling periodic tasks was first addressed by Liu and Layland in 1973. The Liu and Layland analysis was derived under several assumptions: z Tasks are periodic, are ready at the start of each period, have deadlines at the end of the period, and do not suspend themselves during execution. z Tasks can be preempted, and the overhead for context swapping and task scheduling can be ignored. z Tasks are independent, i.e., there is no task synchronization and tasks have known, deterministic worst-case execution times. (2) Rate monotonic scheduling implies that priorities should be assigned to tasks as a monotonically increasing function with respect to the task request rate ) / 1 ( i T . In other words, the more often a task is run, the higher its priority should be. The rate monotonic theory ensures that as long as the processor's utilization is below a certain bound, all tasks in the task set will complete by their deadlines without the individual tasks requiring timing information about the other tasks.

Equations (1) and ( 2) offer a sufficient (worst-case) condition that characterizes schedulability of a task set under the rate monotonic algorithm, in fact, this scheduling policy is too pessimistic to schedule a robotic control task set when the running time of one task changes largely, especially an AI based intelligent algorithm is adopted. To handle the unpredictable characteristic of the running time of the task, in this paper, a feasibility decision function is calculated online for scheduling periodic real-time robotic tasks.

3.2 Scheduling for robotic control task Robot control system is a multi-task real time control system. In our control system there are three periodic tasks, the highest priority task is the motion control task, which performs all low-level sensor sampling and direct motor control. The next highest priority task is the trajectory planning task, which calculate the optimal path according to extern sensor information, e.g. the force & torque sensor. The sensor feedback task has a lower priority which is responsible for sensor information processing. div.head: IV. Robotic Control System and Scheduling Examples
System overview z Air bearing stage for IC packaging
div.p: The 2-DOF air bearing stage presented in this paper is applied to research on hardware, software, controller and foundation theories of high-precision position under highspeed and high-acceleration motion conditions for IC packaging. The characteristics of the 2-DOF stage are generalized parallel mechanism, linear motors direct drive, airbearing sliders and a marble foundation bed. The parallel mechanism is designed to be decoupled, by which interplay between X-axis and Y-axis when moving synchronously can be ignored. Furthermore, two linear motors (IL24_100A1P1 and IL18_100A1P1 produced by Kollmogen Company) drive axes directly in order to obtain high acceleration and large system stiffness, abandoning conventional linear transmission styles which combine rotary motors with ballscrews. High frequency vibration produced by linear direct-drive and preloaded by inclined iron core must be paid attention to. For reducing friction extremely ultra-precision air-bearing stages are designed, in which about 10um thickness air film with certain stiffness between sliders and guides is formed by inputting several million pascals dry air. The air film separates carriages and railways, which realize untouched motion. RGH22 linear encoder system produced by RENISHAW company is adopted for position measurement which resolution is m μ

. An extra Z-axis is added for IC packaging and a 1-DOF force sensor is adopted for force control in packaging process. The system is shown in fig. 5. A standard 4-DOF SCARA type robot is used for assembly processor control. A 6-DOF wrist force-torque sensor is adopted for peg-in-the-hole operation. The system is shown in fig. 6. The extern sensor in the two systems is force sensor, and motion control thread has the highest priority, the algorithm running in the thread includes PD control for inner position loop, disturbance observer, nonlinear friction compensator and gray prediction fuzzy & model prediction algorithm for outer force control loop; the other tasks in this thread are sampling of encoder and force sensor information. The gray prediction fuzzy control algorithm is a time consuming task and the running time is a variable; the trajectory planning thread mainly includes a inverse-kinematic algorithm to form a curve; the sensor feedback thread is to update &display the system information and the user interface thread has a lowest priority for information exchange. In fact, the schedulability analysis is not credible because the policy is too pessimistic. With our research, the actual running time of the force control algorithm is monitored by setting a timer in the motion control thread, according to (3) and ( 4), the experimental results of schedulability decision function will be calculated and shown in fig. 7. It is important to note that the running time of the task includes the running time of algorithm, task creation and task switch. In RTX environment, the task creation and task switch only needs 10-20 s μ , so it is not considered in the calculation of processor utilization.

div.head: V. Conclusion
div.p: In this paper, a PC based open real-time control system and improved rate-monotonic scheduler is designed and implemented, the control software architecture based on Windows NT and its real-time extension-RTX is described in detail. Under the support of the open control system, complex intelligent control algorithms are easy to be embedded to the software. The schedulability of the task set is analyzed and the changing run time of the algorithm is monitored for schedulability decision. Two examples -the air bearing stage for IC packaging and a SCARA robot for assembly are introduced and the scheduling experiment shows that the improved scheduling policy is valid for control algorithm verification.
